notable_absence.finding: 'The basic settings for Couchbase security, available to _Full_ and _Security_ administrators' names an access restriction on the whole Security screen using the bare, unqualified word 'Security' administrators - not the crisper 'Security Admin' label manage-auditing.md uses. Left this as a generic rbac-model:role mention rather than committing it to the role:security-admin id minted in manage-auditing.json, since this page's wording alone does not clearly enough attest the specific named role - flagging the two phrasings as likely the same fact for reconciliation to confirm.

cross_component_finding: This page's own wording for the Certificates panel - 'The Root Certificate for the node, which allows the server to identify itself to clients' - blurs together cert:root-certificate (the CA at the top of a trust chain) and cert:node-certificate (the cert a node itself presents to identify itself), two concepts the registry already keeps deliberately distinct. Quoted and reused cert:root-certificate as the literal term used, but flagging the page's own loose phrasing as a possible source of a 'quotable but mis-objected' relation if reused uncritically downstream.
